7.0.0.en: 1 “When I would have healed Israel, then the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered, and the wickedness of Samaria: for they commit deceit; and the thief cometh in, and the raiders spoil without. 2 And they consider not in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness: now their own doings have beset them about; they are before my face.

7.0.1.en: When God comes forward as a Physician of souls wishing to heal them, He is compelled to declare the sickness and reveal its extent and gravity so that the sick may accept His treatment. “When I would have healed Israel, then the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered, and the wickedness of Samaria: for they commit deceit; and the thief cometh in, and the raiders spoil without” [1].

7.0.2.en: He came to heal Israel in general, and so He declared the iniquity of Ephraim, the tribe that took the first place in evil, and exposed the wickedness of Samaria, which is the capital. He is like a physician who does not flatter or temporize but exposes the sickness so that he may stretch out his hand with the scalpel to cut firmly, yet in love. He declares the iniquity of the most wicked tribe and the most corrupt city without flattery at the expense of healing! As for the kind of sickness that struck them, it is “they commit deceit,” and this is the most dangerous thing that can strike a man, that he practice deceit, deceiving people and perhaps deceiving himself and misleading his conscience, thinking that he is able to deceive God also. His heart is full of robbery while his garments are priestly; his city is like Gilead, in appearance containing the men of God, “the Levites,” but in reality containing “them that work iniquity” (Hos 6:8). Thus Israel cloaked its iniquity by presenting offerings and sacrifices to God and practicing some acts of worship, while its heart was far from God and turned away from Him.

7.0.3.en: If Israel wanted to deceive others with outward appearances, yet the inner corruption bore its reflections on the outward conduct as well, and while it tries to deceive by its appearance it is shattered within and without, for He says: “the thief cometh in, and the raiders spoil without” [1]. The sickness crept in like a thief to the inside, to the hidden depths, and so the door was opened to the raiders outside. Man became corrupt in his entirety, in need of the healing of the heart and thought and intention within, and of treatment of the outward conduct and visible dealings.

7.1.0.en: The most dangerous thing in their sickness is not the sickness itself but their ignoring of it, for they thought it a trivial matter that does not need to be remembered, and that God Himself does not care about it; therefore He says: “they consider not in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness: now their own doings have beset them about; they are before my face” [2]. If their sins are hidden from their eyes, or do not occupy their thought, yet they stand before the face of God, who remembers them in order to remove them from them.

7.1.1.en: Perhaps they ask: Why does God declare the iniquity of Ephraim and expose the wickedness of Samaria? He answers: “now their own doings have beset them about” [2]. It is as though He says to them: Do not be angry with me because I uncover your weaknesses, but rather be angry with yourselves because you walk in this way; for even if I expose, it is only to heal your wounds, but you by ignoring them make your sickness incurable!

7.2.0.en: 3 “They make the king glad with their wickedness, and the princes with their lies. 4 They are all adulterers, as an oven heated by the baker, who ceaseth from raising after he hath kneaded the dough, until it be leavened. 5 In the day of our king the princes have made him sick with the heat of wine; he stretched out his hand with scorners. 6 For they have made ready their heart like an oven, whiles they lie in wait: their baker sleepeth all the night; in the morning it burneth as a flaming fire. 7 They are all hot as an oven, and have devoured their judges; all their kings are fallen: there is none among them that calleth unto me.

7.2.1.en: In chapter four He announced His trial of the priests because of lack of knowledge, and we saw that they represent the heart which, by its impurity, cannot see God, so that it enters with the whole body into the darkness of ignorance and lack of knowledge. Here He condemns the king and the princes, where the king signifies the human will, which by its corruption and evil directs the whole man toward evil and corruption, and the princes signify the centers of leadership in the soul and the energies and gifts they bear.

7.2.2.en: He says: “They make the king glad with their wickedness, and the princes with their lies” [3]. This is the most hideous picture of leadership, which is not only marked by evil but takes pleasure in the evil and lies of others… Therefore He says: “all their kings are fallen: there is none among them that calleth unto me” [7]. It is as though their gladness does not satisfy their lives nor support their souls, but is a temporary, temporal joy that pushes them to fall and deprives them of resorting to God, so they lose the source of their life and true joy.

7.3.0.en: He describes these kings and princes (or the inner leaders of man) in their evil thus: “They are all adulterers, as an oven heated by the baker” [4]. The defiled soul becomes like a burning oven, inflamed by evil lusts and uncontrolled passions. St. Jerome says: [“They are all adulterers, their hearts are like an oven” (Septuagint), like an oven which the mercies of God, together with strict fasting, cannot quench (because of their lack of repentance). These are the fiery darts (Eph 6:16) with which Satan wounds men and makes them as though in fire, this fire which the king of Babylon kindled against the three young men… but a fourth appeared in the form of the Son of God, calming the terrible heat and making the flame of the fiery furnace cold.]

7.3.1.en: St. Jerome holds that this fiery furnace, kindled by evil lusts, can be quenched only by the fiery Holy Spirit, who burns up the corrupt fire in order to kindle God’s holy fire within the heart, for he says: [If the heart were not kindled by the Holy Spirit it could not overcome lust, for the Spirit of the Lord kindled it and burned up the fire of lust]! He also speaks of the holy fire, saying: [Let us pray to the Lord who turns any hardness in us into gentleness, and blots out our sins, so that we become like fire, the coldness of the devil in our heart is removed from us and we grow in the warmth of the Holy Spirit, thus even with the presence also of intense heat of course…]

7.4.0.en: Not only did they themselves become a burning oven, but even their hidden evil plots and schemes become like the oven: “For they have made ready their heart like an oven, whiles they lie in wait: their baker sleepeth all the night; in the morning it burneth as a flaming fire” [6]. Just as the baker throws wood into the oven and goes to sleep at night and finds it in the morning blazing, so these wicked men throw in fuel, the evil counsels, and in dullness sleep all their night, and at the right time they find the oven blazing.

7.5.0.en: “They are all hot as an oven, and have devoured their judges” [7]. They devoured the very few righteous who condemn their evil conduct… They became a devouring fire not to evil but to the just judges.

7.6.0.en: 8 “Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned. 9 Strangers have devoured his wealth, and he knoweth it not: yea, gray hairs are sprinkled upon him, yet he knoweth not. 10 And the pride of Israel is humbled in his face: and they do not return to the LORD their God, nor seek him for all this. 11 Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria. 12 When they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven; I will chastise them according to the report of their congregation.

7.6.1.en: Having uncovered the leaders who became like a heated oven inflamed with the fuel of evil lusts, devouring their righteous judges, He uncovers to the people also their sickness, saying:

7.6.2.en: A. “Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned” [8]. The boundaries that separate Ephraim from the pagan peoples were removed, although God had earlier affirmed: “The people shall dwell alone” (Num 23:9), but they “were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works” (Ps 106:35). It is a bitter picture of a Church that bears the spirit of the world within her, does not know her obligation as a servant of the Kingdom, but lives with an earthly, temporal mind. Truly it is fitting for the Church not to withdraw from the world in pride nor to take the stance of one who justifies herself, but to bow down like her Lord in love to wash every foot, and open her heart to every person, and show tenderness toward every human being, in order to lift all up to the heavenly life, and not to come down herself to earthly, fleshly thinking.

7.6.3.en: As for his saying, “a cake not turned,” it refers to the bread that was not turned before being put into the oven, so that its outside appears leavened while the lower part is unleavened; therefore when it enters the oven the upper part cracks while the lower part becomes “heavy and not light.” Thus Ephraim has a religious face when he presents sacrifices and offerings and acts of devotion, but the hidden face bears apostasy from God. Hypocrisy makes man “a cake not turned”: what the public face shows is contrary to what the hidden face bears.

7.6.4.en: The wicked man, especially the hypocrite, is likened to a cake not turned, which the devil, as a baker, puts into the oven heated and inflamed with the fire of lusts. Whereas the Lord Christ enters with His body into the oven of His divine love, bearing in it the wounds of love and the marks of the Cross in order to present Him to us as “the bread which came down from heaven” (Jn 6), the devil on the contrary wants to catch us in order to put us into the oven of his evil and make of us a cake not turned that he desires and plays with and mocks!

7.7.0.en: B. “Strangers have devoured his wealth, and he knoweth it not” [9]. Who are these strangers if not the kings of the nations on whom the people of God leaned (relied) to save them, and behold, they devoured them and plundered them of their wealth, as “the king of Syria made them like the dust to be trodden” (2 Kgs 13:7). And as Pharaoh of Egypt also did to them, and the kings of Assyria… so whoever does not return to God his Savior becomes plunder for strangers.

7.7.1.en: These strangers are in reality the devil and his demons and his works (sins), for they take captive the soul that opens the door to them and plunder from it the most precious thing it has, its eternal life. Thus the devil is counted a stranger because he is not the Creator, yet he claims the world for himself, and wants to possess every soul to make of it a cake not turned, taking it into his oven heated with fire in order to devour it and play with it!

7.7.2.en: C. “Yea, gray hairs are sprinkled upon him, yet he knoweth not” [9], that is, gray hair spread over their heads and they do not realize… They entered into a state of spiritual old age and came near to decay (Heb 8:13), and as Abba Moses says: [There are some who passed into old age through lukewarmness and sloth.]

7.7.3.en: But the godly believer’s heart never grows old, but even if his outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed day by day (2 Cor 4:16); he is like the eagle whose youth is renewed (Ps 103:5). Such a one bears not the gray hair of the head or the heart that shatters the body or the soul, but the gray hair of wisdom, that is, its long experience, as the wise man says: “For the gray hair of man is prudence, and the age of old age is the unblemished life; it is not by gray hair of the head but by the wisdom of the virtuous life, and the attaining of the way of perfection in Christ Jesus our Lord.

7.8.0.en: D. Their fall into pride and self-reliance instead of reliance on God: “And the pride of Israel is humbled in his face: and they do not return to the LORD their God, nor seek him for all this” [10], which He had reproved them for earlier (Hos 5:5).

7.9.0.en: E. “Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria” [11]. The kingdom of Israel was thus constantly floundering; it left its true nest, “the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem,” and went to Samaria to set up a temple according to its own whim. And behold, now it flounders, at one time going to Pharaoh of Egypt to ally with him against the king of Assyria, and at another doing the opposite, and both exploit it for their own account.

7.9.1.en: It is a silly dove without dignity or wisdom, and without heart, for it bears no spirit of love for God, who draws it to the heavens in one direction without floundering. But the true Church is a dove in the clefts of the rock (Song 2:14), hidden in the Lord Christ, the Rock of ages, walking with dignity and wisdom and bearing a heart wide enough for the love of the heavenly and earthly alike!

7.9.2.en: St. Jerome comments on the verse before us, saying: [Note that he compares Ephraim to a foolish dove, since Ephraim left the temple and dwelt in the forests. For doves always live in towers, but Ephraim, my dove, abandoned the temple, left the house to live in the forests, and so came to dwell in the wilderness.]

7.9.3.en: May we not be like the silly dove that knows no resting place, but enter into the Lord through His holy altar and meet Him in His sacrifice that grants salvation, saying: “Yea, the sparrow hath found an house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, even thine altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God. Blessed are they that dwell in thy house: they will be ever praising thee” (Ps 84:3-4).

7.10.0.en: 13 “Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: ruin unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I redeem them, yet they have spoken lies against me. 14 And they have not cried unto me with their heart, when they howled upon their beds: they assemble themselves for corn and wine, and they turn away from me. 15 Though I warned them and strengthened their arms, yet do they imagine mischief against me. 16 They return, but not to the most High: they are like a bow that misses: their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue: this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.

7.10.1.en: Since the heavenly Physician affirmed the necessity of uncovering the wounds and declaring the sickness, for the leaders as for the people, they could not bear this, and declared their rebellion against Him. “Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: ruin unto them! because they have transgressed against me” [13]. He was gracious to them to heal them, and they counted Him an enemy, and fled from Him as the silly dove flees from the towers to live wandering without shelter, and thereby they insulted God their Shepherd and transgressed against Him. They met His love with disobedience, and His gentleness with enmity, for He rebukes them, saying: “though I redeem them, yet they have spoken lies against me” [13]. What is the lie they spoke against God? When they fell into distress they returned with a lie, and did not return to Him in truth, for they returned to have the distress removed from them, while their hearts clung to deviation… They came for temporal blessings of corn and wine, but their hearts turned away from the Giver of gifts. “And they have not cried unto me with their heart, when they howled upon their beds: they assemble themselves for corn and wine (because the rain was withheld from them), and they turn away from me” [14].

7.10.2.en: They used to cry out with their lips with many words, while their hearts were far from God, whereas, on the contrary, we see Moses not uttering a word with his lips, and God hears the cries of his inner heart (Ex 14:15) and answers them.

7.11.0.en: God supports them and strengthens their arms, but they imagine mischief against Him [15]; therefore they do not return to the Most High nor seek Him with their hearts, but only through outward appearances. “They are like a bow that misses”… they gather together and cry out, but instead of striking the enemy with bow and sword they shatter themselves and their inner energies: “their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue” [16].

7.12.0.en: “This shall be their derision in the land of Egypt” [16], for they flee to Pharaoh and take refuge in him, and so become an object of mockery and scorn because God has withdrawn from them.
